content.title: About
content.content: Textured vegetable protein (TVP), dry, is a defatted soy protein obtained from soybeans. It has a porous, meat‑like texture and is used as a meat substitute in vegetarian and vegan dishes. TVP has a neutral flavor, allowing it to absorb the taste of sauces and seasonings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: TVP is produced by extrusion, where soy protein is forced through a die under high pressure and temperature.
It is often called “soy meat” or “soy chunks.”
Dry TVP has a long shelf life – up to 2 years when stored in a dry place.
It contains about 50 % protein and virtually no fat, making it popular among athletes.
TVP rehydrates quickly in water or broth within 5‑10 minutes.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: TVP provides roughly 50 % protein by dry weight, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: It contains almost no saturated fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Soy protein is rich in these trace minerals important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in TVP promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Supports vegetarian and vegan diets
items.content: A complete plant‑based protein source without animal products.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: People allergic to soy may experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylaxis when consuming TVP.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; combine TVP with vitamin C‑rich foods to mitigate this.

items.title: Genetically modified organisms (GMO)
items.content: Most soy crops are GMO; choose non‑GMO certified products if required.

items.title: Sodium in seasoned varieties
items.content: Some flavored TVP mixes contain added salt; check labels if monitoring sodium intake.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Before cooking, soak dry TVP in hot water or broth for 5‑10 minutes, then drain. Use it in stews, sauces, veggie burgers, tacos, chili, or add to casseroles. Its neutral taste lets it take on any seasoning or sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry TVP in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent moisture absorption and quality loss.
